attributes.residual: Unchanged from the prior pass and now measured more precisely: insns 215/215, opcode multiset IDENTICAL, frame 88 and save-set stmw r29 both matching target. Six blocking words, all stack-displacement immediates, in the two groups itemised in the axis log; everything else in the function is an FPR/GPR renaming. WEBFRANK: NOT ELIGIBLE and cannot be made eligible by a rule. A displacement is an IMMEDIATE field, which register_slot_mask excludes by construction (that is exactly why these six words are reported as 'non-register instruction bits differ'), and the registered tool constraints forbid using WebFrank for immediate differences outright. So no pin can be authored for this function while any slot delta survives - the slots must be closed at the SOURCE first, after which the remaining pure renaming would become a legitimate copy_register_fields candidate. THE NAMED NEXT STEP, and it is OUT OF THIS LANE'S SCOPE: `tmp` is pinned to the top of the local region across FOUR distinct axes now (inner-block scope and function scope from the prior pass, pad relocation and conserving pad re-split from this one). The pad is not the lever and should not be probed again. The untried idea is that `volatile f32 tmp` is itself the fakematch: it is a hand-written device to force the f64->f32 truncation round-trip through memory, and the original 2001 source almost certainly just assigned the f32 expression and let MWCC allocate its OWN truncation temp - which is plausibly the slot target places at 0x14. Removing the volatile local and writing the natural assignment is the axis to try, and it is a change to move_logic15's BODY, which this closure lane's work claim explicitly forbids (pad/declaration only). Hand to the lane owning game/enemy/enemy.
